content: Prologue The first age of man ended much as it had begun…with silence.  At the close of the 22 nd  century, earth stood empty, bereft of humans, void of their monuments. The beasts once again ruled the planet. The instrument of man’s demise, the alien weapon, found beneath the ice of the planet, now stood as the last guardian to technology on the small blue world.  Though Earth stood empty of man, the universe did not. Seeing the end coming, mankind, in a last desperate act to save itself, created the ARC.  Altered with knowledge learned from the alien weapon, it gave mankind the ability to safely enter a deep frozen state of slumber and awaken centuries later, the last remnants of mankind, twenty thousand souls in all, slept away the ages, aboard the large ship as it floated out near mars, until it was safe to once again step foot upon the globe. The grand ARC, man’s best hope for a future, eventually returned to the little blue planet, the last evidence of man’s mastery over machine, stood sentry over the small blue planet.  The ships artificial intelligence watched and waited, the machine standing vigil, analyzing and scanning the world man once called home. Only once the world was once again deemed safe were the PODS release back to the now-feral world, the slumbering inheritors of man’s destiny.  Still frozen in the small pods that would be fired back to the planet, allowing man once again to take their rightful place upon the Earth.  However, some did not return. Either by accident or some purpose not understood by man or machine, they floated above the planet, locked in orbit, locked in sleep, randomly falling to the world as the  ages  past.  This is the story of one such sleeper… ONE M A R C U S Honor is the first of the four tenants.  It is the measure by which all men are judged. -Book of Aurtus  “Am I home?” The unfamiliar voice spoke causing Marcus to pause in surprise, that isn’t me is it he wondered, blinking back the painful sunlight, his vision beginning to clear as the green and brown of the cold autumn forest came into focus, looking up he surveyed the surviving leaves playing in the cold breeze as it drifted across the canopy. Earth, he thought as his body began to relax, the deep ache from joints that had not been moved in centuries called to him as he shifted.  Turning he studied the remnants of the silver teardrop shaped craft half buried at the end of a long ravine created when it had hit the ground. How long have I been away? He wondered looking to the surrounding fauna for answers, but none came. Marcus winced as his muscles protested in pain as he moved them, testing his strength. The one-piece gortex outfit he wore stretching with the movements of his body, the restriction of the outfit causing him to scowl in annoyance.  After such a long period of Cryogenic sleep, your body will require a period of time to adjust, though your entire being will be frozen, ensuring you do not age while waiting for your return home we anticipate certain unpleasant side effects that you will have to overcome upon awakening  a familiar voice echoed from his mind, a holdover from his now distant past.  Here I am  he thought, a smile replacing the annoyed wince as he studied the lush green landscape before him.  Marcus had spent time in forests, mostly training with the Army, but it had not been a place he had felt at home. In fact, during his time with the Army Corp of Engineers he had spent most of his time in the deserts of Africa, engineering irrigation solutions for small remote areas. The forest though familiar was not the comfort he had hoped it would be.  He continued to sit for a moment, not trusting his muscles to stand, he missed the desert, missed the work, he had been good at it, in fact it had been his reputation of solving unsolvable problems that had brought him to the attention of the ARC project. Marcus shook his head as memories flooded his mind, the machine found in the ice, the discovery of its purpose as a weapon and then the panic, The ARC project had been formed as a last ditch effort, they had studied the machine, learned from it and then applied some of that technology to allow mankind the ability to launch into space and sleep away centuries as it waited for the plant to heal.  “Here I am” he said, again the gravelly voice damn near unrecognizable to him. He shook it off as he unsteadily got to his feet. Shuffling over to the ship he leaned down and studied the damage to the hull it isn’t going to fly again he thought walking around the small vessel, the pod that had returned him to the planet and for a moment he looked up, he imagined for a moment he could see the large mothership that hovered in geosynchronous orbit, pods lined up in there docks as they waited for the Artificial Intelligence to deem the planet safe and begin launch sequence.  He had spent centuries on board that ship, sleeping, frozen, just waiting for the computer to finally launch him and all his fellow volunteers back to the planet that has birthed humanity. Turning with a start as something large moved through the woods some distance away, he felt fear creep up his back and shambled his way towards the rear of the teardrop shaped ship. He might have been trained as a soldier, but Marcus Gavin had spent his career building and creating, not fighting what few combat skills he had were remnants of the training he had once received in Basic training.  Reaching the back of the small vessel he breathed a sigh a relief to see that the rear section had been undamaged. Marcus listened for another tell-tale sign of the large creature in the woods, but none came, Feeling around the surface of the vessel he found the small indent he had been looking for and pushed, a recessed keyboard slid smoothly from the ship and he tapped in a code , waiting patiently as a door slid open , revealing a packed storage compartment. He began pulling out he gear stored there, mostly emergency supplies should he find himself far from civilization, a backpack, a tent, food and stored water all of which he stacked neatly next to the ship.  Reaching into the rear of the compartment Marcus smiled as his hand closed over a large black plastic case. Sliding it out, he opened it to reveal a Military issue carbine and pistol, complete with extra clips stored nearly in the padded case. Picking up the carbine and a magazine he loaded the weapon, pulling back the charging handle and letting it slam forward, the metal on metal sound of a bullet being chambered comforting as he moved around the ship and faced the direction of the sound.  After some deliberation, he decided a warning shot would be the most effective and pointed the rifle at a large tree and aimed, squeezing the trigger he was surprised when the only sound was the metallic click. Pulling his cheek off of the stock, he studied the weapon curiously for a moment, then he ejected the round and chambered another, squeezing the trigger, once again was rewarded with a metallic click. “What the hell” he whispered looking at the weapon.  His voice sounding at least semi normal he thought distractedly. Pulling the magazine, he popped a round out of the magazine and proceeded to rummage around in the overloaded pack until he came out with a small tool case. Carefully he removed the round from the shell and upending the metal casing a small clump of yellowish rock tumbled out of the bullet casing. “Of all the stupid upgrades” he chastised no one in particular, recalling one briefing he remembered the excitement of the engineer when they had revealed that the cordite mixture might not last centuries and they had come up with a solution to that problem.  As Marcus stared at the useless rock in his hand, he simply shook his head, the guns were useless he realized and packing it away he began searching the equipment for anything else he could use. Within twenty minutes he had laid out an Ontario K-Bar knife and a survival hatched. Judging by the sound of the thing in the woods, if it was hostile this wouldn’t do more than piss it off, he thought but it was better than nothing. He had spent his entire military career being a creator, a problem solder not a killer, not a destroyer he thought.  Which is why at the young age of twenty seven he had already developed a reputation in both the Army and the private sector as the go to person when an engineering problem had been too daunting or unsolvable, He had always managed to find a solution and implement it much to the amazement of his superiors and his peers.  Marcus stripped out of the wet chemical covered one piece outfit and into more traditional army BDU’s doing his best to wipe away the chemicals that covered his body head to do, the mixture that had assisted in his cryogenic sleep now merely an annoyance, much like the birth fluid on a new born he thought, running a spare t-shirt through his hair to remove as much of the sticky substance as possible. Standing there clean and dry he took a deep appreciative breath of the clean forest air, he knew the plan, the scenario and was pleased to see the surrounding woods untouched by what they thought would be the end of the planet.  When they had found the machine, the scientists in charge of studying it had not known what it was they had when during an experiment had inadvertently activated the damn thing. It had taken another year to finally figure out what it was that they had turned on and more importantly how to read the countdown that had begun on that fateful day. In their efforts they had lost a year out of six, leaving five years before the machine would destroy mankind, releasing virulent pathogens and nanite armies to remove humans and their creations.  Shortly thereafter the ARC project was started, taking technology learned from the machine,  they began to build ships, technologies and the process of placing humans in Cryonic sleep, freezing them until such time that they would return. But if Marcus knew that would happen in batches, meaning he wouldn’t be the only one who would have returned he thought, looking around and seeing no sign of another pod or human. He needed information he thought reaching into the pod and from the center of the control system removed a metallic object that looked like a chrome egg, another piece of that altered technology he thought, placing the small device on the ground as it began to pulse red. Standing and watching it, he waited as the red lights turned yellow and then a solid green, once it had made its connection with the mothership above, the small egg began to raise off of the ground, coming to float at eye level, as Marcus watched a person began to form around the device first as a wireframe and then filling out as the holo projectors activated, eventually leaving a dark silver silhouette of a person standing in front of him.  “Sentinel is online Marcus Gavin, by your command” the soft female voice stated and he sighed, at least the VI worked he thought, the device when he had first seen it , had been confusing it was a simple virtual interface, without an intelligence of its own, the device would connect to the ship, allowing the Artificial intelligence there to interact with a volunteer, thus like a puppet for the AI, it would give him an interface to communicate with the ship and hopefully other volunteers he thought.  “Sentinel, please review mission and bring me up to speed on the current situation” he stated clearly, as he watched the silhouette froze for a minute, the device communicating and receiving information from the ship, the distance causing a small lag in response he knew. Finally, the VI shook its head “Certainly Marcus” it began, and the image of the person vanished, forming instead into an image of the planet hanging in front of him. He knew it was from the ships archives, the image centuries old, from when the mission began but still seeing Earth and all its lights and people from space caused his breath to pause, it was his home he thought, watching as the planet lazily spun in front of him.  After a moment it began to speed up the AI giving a time-lapsed image and as Marcus watched, ships launched from the surface and quickly began to load into the mothership, that had been the pods, they had loaded everyone into them on earth and then like cargo shipped the frozen volunteers to the mothership, loading them into the berths. The flurry of activity stopped, and the earth continued to spin, the rotation speeding up even more as the AI accelerated the view once again.  Then to Marcus’s horror the lights on the planet began to go out, slow at first and then faster and faster, before long the planet was dark, a red mist began to populate the planet leaving it in a red haze, he didn’t know what it was but decided to wait to ask, instead allowing the visual briefing to continue, eventually the red haze faded as the planet spun, faster and faster. For almost thirty minutes it did it, the planet a blur until instantly it slowed and as Marcus watched, pods exploded from the mothership and began to descend to earth, as he watched a second and then a third mothership came into view and those two launched its pods, the small metal ships descending to earth, then the planet sped up again, slowing once in a while as a random pod launched, then it would speed up again repeating the process a little time later, this happened twelve times, until a final pod launched, descending to earth and the visual briefing stopped.  Marcus stood there silent as he thought through what he just witnessed, what had he seen, he wondered, playing it back  In  his head. “Sentinel, what can you tell me about the red dust that was released over the planet” he said and waited as the earth dissolved and yet again the silhouette reappeared in front of him. “From our sensors, it was a swarn of nanite machines, its purpose was to deconstruct any artificial construct on the planet, once done the swarm eventually died, however our records indicate a large growth of crystalline formations growing over the planet after that time, these formations then began to pulse with a frequency that has since interfered with our ability to document and record from the planet surface.  Again  Marcus paused, looking around he finaly noticed small crystal growths on the trees and ground, the red, blue and green crystal spires seeming to grow on anything. He stepped over and bend  down to study a spire, It looked harmless he thought and reaching out, touched it with his finger, just as quickly he pulled it away, as if the rock had bit him, slowly Marcus reached out again and touched the rock, it thrummed as if power was coursing through the small rock, he could feel the vibration into his fingers and hand, After a moment he pulled his hand away, as he tried to count how many crystals he could see, Marcus quickly lost count at a thousand, almost every tree had at least one he thought, such an invasive species and shaking his head he turned back to the VI “Are they powered, or are the crystals emitting some sort of signal” he asked and again the VI paused as it communicated with the AI on his mothership.  “Yes to both questions, there is a sort of power emanating through them but the source is unknown and they are operating on a wavelength, sending out a low level communications, though it is too low to reach orbit and only seems effective up to a thousand feet from the crystal itself, the signal is constant so it is more of a simple hum then anything intelligent” Sentinel finished.  Marcus shook his head again looking back to the crystal, that was an interesting mystery, but one outside of his expertise he thought. “Sentinel why launch random pods after the initial exodus?” he asked, remembering the lone pods launched over time. He waited for a response. “Due to a malfunction , over thirty pods remained on the ship, as they were repaired, they were then launched and returned to earth, as of this time twelve of the thirty have been returned over a period of three centuries” the VI finished and Marcus shook his head not believing what he had just heard “Sentinel, what is the reason for the timeframe, surely it has not taken that long to fix twelve pods?” he asked , something wasn’t right but this was a machine, not made to be malicious or nefarious he reassured himself.  The VI paused, this time longer than normal when it came back the silhouette shrugged in a very human manner that caused Marcus to almost take a step back at the action. “That is unknown, the answer to that question is not available beyond administration level access” Sentinel stated, and Marcus narrowed his eyes, since when did a repair get top level access only, he wondered.  “Sentinel, who authorized the change in security for the repair information?” he asked and again waited for the machine’s answer “That information is not available beyond administration level access” the machine stated the tone that of an instructor reciting the rules to a particularly dense student.  Marcus shook his head, he would have to look at that later, this brought up other issues he thought. “Sentinel, I assume the last pod to return was mine, what is the timeframe from the exodus to my pod returning to the planet” he asked, but he had seen the briefing and new well he wouldn’t like the answer.  After a moment Sentinel came back “Two hundred twelve years since exodus” she said, and it felt as if the breath was knocked out of his chest and Marcus stumbled back. Two hundred years, people have been on the planet for two centuries he thought, and he was just now returning, what the hell happened he wondered. More importantly, where was everyone, why had no one come to welcome him he wondered, Thinking through his options he nodded and queried Sentinel again. “Sentinel, can you scan the surrounding area for populations, civilization or communication of any kind, purpose is to find a concentration of people” he finished and waited with bated breath as the VI paused, communication with the ship and gathering those results.  Sentinel returned quicker than he expected “Marcus because of the interference, I am unable to lock on any location of a human population, however I can tell you that there are no communications either over this location or the entire North American continent, no digital or analog broadcasts have been detected since the exodus itself” Sentinel stated, again causing Marcus to pause in an alarmed panic.  How can that be he thought, people have been back for two hundred years, with the supplies and expertise of the twenty thousand people returned, surely there would be some sort of civilization he wondered, the information bothering him. Were there still people left he wondered, could the  effects of the machine have lasted causing those that returned to have died his mind continued.  That’s not helpful he chastised himself beginning to pace, he needed a plan, he couldn’t stay out here in the woods waiting for someone to come and get him. He was no survivalist, he was a damn engineer, aside from basic classes he had no real ability to survive in the woods for long periods of time he thought, suddenly thinking maybe he should have gone to ranger school when he had the change.  After a few minutes of pacing he had not come up with anything that could even be considered a plan. With a sigh he turned back to the VI “Sentinel, based on the current information do you have a suggestion for a course of action that will allow me to learn the disposition and possibly reconnect with the population on the planet” he asked and with a mental wince, waited for the answer. A moment later the VI nodded “Marcus, based on the limited information we have it is my suggestion that the first place to stop would be the supply bunkers, you have limited supplies and since it could some time to local others, you will need to ensure your ability to survive” The VI stated calmly and Marcus could have slapped himself on the forehead.  “Of Course” He mumbled  “The damn bunkers” , during the planning phase of the project, the ARC leaders had set about building bunkers throughout the western united states, where the volunteers would later land to rebuild, knowing the ships couldn’t carry the supplies and the status of the planet would be unknown, bunkers were created to ensure that the equipment, supplies and food would be available to the volunteers upon their return. Marcus knew it was a long shot, he was two centuries late to the party, it was very possible that those bunkers would be empty, but maybe there would be a clue as to where the volunteers had done. Either way he thought, it was a good idea “Sentinel, prepare to guide me to the closets bunker” Marcus commanded and began to collect his supplies.  As the sun began to descend over the canopy , bringing dusk to the forest, Marcus dropped the pack with a grunt, Sentinel walked over to the tree , standing there and waiting for orders, as he collapsed upon the pack and eyed the VI , he knew it didn’t really walk, the device simply floating as it gave the appearance its hologram was walking with him. For the entire day he had followed the damn VI as they navigated the forest westward towards the closest bunker to his ships landing site. He had covered the ship with dead branches, doing his best to hide it, he wasn’t sure from what or whom, but it seemed like a good idea at the time he thought, but the exertion of doing that on top of walking made him rethink his earlier decision. “Sentinel, when will we reach the bunker” he asked, playing his own little game of ‘are we there yet’ with the machine.  “We will reach the bunker tomorrow at noon based on our days progress” Sentinel stated and with a grunt, Marcus nodded as he began to remove the tent and set it up, after clumsily setting up his camp and finally getting a fire started, he was heating a small can of corn beef hash, one of the few heavy food supplies that he had when a rustling from the trees caught his attention. Standing he pulled the hatchet and scanned the canopy as more branches shivered with movement. Something was up there he thought taking a step back, never taking his eyes off of the tree.  He almost jumped out of his skin when a black tendril broke free of the densely covered branch and took off across the expanse towards another tree, stopping halfway and simply hovering as it waited for something. Marcus stood there, his jaw agape and the hatchet forgotten as he studied the creature, now fully displayed in the waning sunlight of the day. “Sentinel, can you scan that creature” he whispered and waited as the VI put its palm up, virtual windows appearing into existence as the device began to scan the area.  Leaving Marcus to study it.  It is a snake he thought, following the black scaly body, which measured about six feet in length, ending at a narrow snakes head, that wasn’t what bothered him he reflected, his eyes now focusing on the bat like wings sprouting from halfway along its body, the membranous wings lazily flapping as they cupped the air , keeping the animal in the air. “What the hell” he breathed, not able to take his eyes from the creature.  “Marcus, it appears to be some kind of hybrid animal, it is not the only one as others of its kind are close by, I would say from the number that this is not a fluke but a mutation in the animal , one that has evolved to become the species” Sentinel stated, loud enough to startle the creature and send it flying  into the far tree line, just as quickly about ten more erupted from the first tree and joined it, the flock moving at a fast speed to join its compatriot. “Well it seems some things have changed since my last time here” he said half astonished and half smiling at his weak joke.  The next day as the sun finished its climb to mid-day Marcus found himself standing at the base of a large hill, the churned earth having settled long ago from the looks of it “Where are we Sentinel?” he asked looking around , searching for signs of the large warehouse like bunker that should be here.  For a few moments the VI stood stalwart before moving again towards the large mound of dirt “The bunker is directly in front of us based on the coordinates in the system” she said floating up the berm, Marcus scrambled to follow. Shaking his head he struggled to climb the simple slope a headache that had plagued him all morning getting worse, a hum had started early that morning and the more they had walked the worse it had gotten, here at the base of the hill it almost felt as if his entire cranium were vibrating, as if something he were following a sound and it had begun to get worse.  Making it to the top he stood there looking over the expanse and marveled at the large hole filled to the brim with crystal spires, all colors and all sizes, the spires reaching from the deep pit towards the sky, as if someone had lined the entire thing with spikes to kill a giant he thought staring in disbelief at the sheer amount of the rocks.  “This is not possible, according to my coordinates this is the location of the closest bunker Marcus” Sentinel stated, her palm outstretched as she began gathering readings from the enormous collection of crystals.  Marcus merely sat on the edge rubbing his head as the thrumming seemed worse here, what the hell is that he wondered squinting from the pain at the large hole of colorful rocks. After a moment he slid down the side of the hill and walked a small distance from the crater sized hole, the further he was from the collection of crystals the quieter his head became.  Finally once he had reached a distance where he could begin to think Marcus began to pace, he was a problem solver, his abilities relied in recognizing patterns others missed and something in the back of his mind was going off, was it something that sentinel had said that morning he wondered, continuing to wear a track in the forest floor as he concentrated on what he had learned from the machine over the past few days.  There was something there about the crystals and power, something about a signal, that might explain the feeling in his head, was it possible that he could sense the power or the signal, similar to some who were able to sense powerlines the closer they came to them he wondered. He was side tracking himself and knew it, that wasn’t what was bothering him.  Finally pausing in mid motion, he turned to the VI image “Sentinel, didn’t you say that the crystals appeared after the dissipation of the red nanite swarm?” he asked, knowing there was a correlation there, pulling on the thread of thought, he tried to follow it to its conclusion.  After a momentary pause the VI returned “Yes Marcus, why do you ask?” it queried, with a simple nod he continued to pace, continued to think through the thought as it began to coalesce in his mind. “Sentinel scan the makeup of the crystals in that crater and then match it to the known chemical components of what would have been in that bunker” Marcus stated, crossing his fingers that he was wrong. It took almost fifteen minutes before the VI returned “It was not easy, the crystals themselves making remote scanning next to impossible, but this unit was able to collect enough local data to do an extrapolation” it began as Marcus waited impatiently for his answer. “According to the scan, the chemical makeup of the crystal collection matches that of the makeup of the building and supplies within the bunker at eighty seven percent” Sentinel finished and waited for Marcus’s next command.  Blowing out a breath he eyed the trees around him seeing the crystal growths, and finally  knowing what he was looking at, what those beautiful monoliths represented. “Sentinel, I think we are looking at what was left of the human race, I think we are seeing what happened to the components of every building, monument, food wrapper and who knows what else that the swarm destroyed, I think these crystals are the tombstone to our race” he finished still eyeing the crystals. Sentinel did not respond, simple stood there waiting for the next order, despite the epiphany that Marcus had just laid on them both.  Suddenly he felt tired, drained of whatever energy remained in him, sitting down he hung his head, thinking of all that had been taken from this world, taken from him as he continued to stare at the innocent looking crystal. As he sat there, a movement caught his eye, looking to his left he watched as a small mound of crystal spires began to move through the forest floor, he couldn’t believe it , was it possible that the crystals themselves were alive he wondered, slowing getting up and watching as the mound continued to move. He crept over, slowly as the mound moved once again, making his way over, Marcus peered down into the semi tall grass and began to laugh, under the mound of crystals rose a very familiar site, the heard of a turtle rising from beneath the ornate shell.  “That’s a lot of bling my friend” he laughed shaking his head. The turtle did not seem impressed with his observation and continued to move towards the safety of the trees as Marcus continued to study the crystal shell. “Sentinel” he called and the VI walked over to stand next to him “Can you scan this, is this shell covered with crystal growths?” he asked and Sentinel stooped down, running its hand over the shell as new windows appeared in midair, listing information and graphs, the data being transmitted to the ship, analyzed and then returned.  Sentinel stood and turned to Marcus “It appears that the shell is crystal Marcus, after a quick scan it appears that this creature’s DNA has been altered as was the snakes” it stated. That alone wiped the smile from his face, Were the crystals somehow changing the animal life on the planet he wondered, then recalled the changes to his own body that the ARC project had propagated in order to allow him and all. The volunteers to survive cryogenic sleep, changes that had gotten from biological compounds found within the machine itself.  With another swell of fear forming he turned to the VI “Sentinel , scan me and tell me if the alterations that were completed at ARC have any similarity to the changes happening to the animals on Earth” he said, praying to anyone that would listen to ensure he was wrong in his assumption. After a few minutes Sentinel spoke “There are some similarities to the changes that were made to your own DNA, but they are rudimentary at best in matching it to the fauna on this planet, when taken into account the vast differences in the DNA you have requested an analysis of” it stated and Marcus almost breathed a sigh of relief, pausing as a thought shot through his mind causing him to wince “Sentinel, extrapolate for changes over time and tell me how similar the changes would be to say this turtle a few centuries from now” he said and again waited, hoping he was wrong.  Sentinel returned after a time “Good assumption Marcus , the changes to your own DNA bear very similar markers to ones that theoretically will occur over most of the animal population of the planet in four centuries but again, the exact nature of the changes cannot be determined because there is no one to one comparison” Sentinel finished and Marcus winced again, somehow whatever changes the ARC project had given him with the advanced DNA manipulation were some kind of blue print to whatever would happen to the animals here.  That brought up a few unpleasant thoughts he reflected “Sentinel, based on the information you have at the time communications were cut off from Earth, did they surmise a function for the machine?” he asked. Thinking he knew what they would have found. “Yes Marcus, according to the. Records, the final theory prior to communications being cut was that the device was not a weapon at all, but an advanced tera former” she finished.  Whatever had built the damn thing thought Marcus had set it upon his planet to ensure that it would eventually be habitable for their form of life, why so long he wondered, surely with the  technology that he had seen, the machine. Could have simply altered the planet and the species, why go through slow changes he wondered. He had a few theories but nothing he could prove, besides he had more important problems he thought.  Marcus setup camp once again, but instead of settling in, he began pacing, he had to find people, had to find out what happened to original volunteers, had they succeeded and there was a civilization for him to return to , or had they simply died off, leaving Marcus the sole hier to humanity. He wondered.  He paced most of the afternoon trying to solve the problem of the sensors, but the more he thought about it the more frustrated he became, he was a mechanical engineer, not a damn software engineer, if there was a problem that required the sensors to be calibrated, he wasn’t the man to do it, he admitted slumping down in defeat next to the tent.  As the sun settled behind the horizon, the autumn air grew a bite as it became colder. Lighting a fire he huddled next to it sulking in his thoughts, He had failed , there was no way to use the ship to locate humans he thought, he would be forced to wander aimlessly hoping to run into a village or city he thought, pulling out a can, he turned to find a general label for beef stew “Last can before we get to the pouch food” he said.  The cans had not been standard issue, but frozen in vacuum they would not go bad so, he and a few others had snuck them in prior to packing the bags for the trip. He recalled the night that he and a few others laughing at threw in the can’s, thinking they would share them once they had awoken. Sitting alone he grew deeper into depression at the thought of those few people now long dead, centuries ago and yet here he sat, alone and eating.  He lay leaning against a tree, the final embers of the firelight casting shadows across the ground and tent as if a kabuki show were in progress for his entertainment. Closing his eyes he breathed out, his body and mind were still recovering from the frozen centuries of sleep but yet he had to push himself, had to find others, his limited supplies meant that sooner or later he would have to find a way to feed himself out here or find a town or people to aid him. If he were honest with himself, he was scared, scared of being alone, scared of being the last human on earth, fated to wander the wilderness until he died. That thought did not sit well with him, he had been lost in his thoughts when a light shot above him, moving from branch to branch and catching his attention.  With a light groan he lifted himself from the tree as his joints protested the interruption from there rest. Studying the canopy above he caught another light as it moved between the branches, as if flying between trees, his sore joints were soon forgotten as he continued to follow the strange lights, sometimes alone and other times grouped in three or four.  “What the hell are you?” he whispered , trying to get a look at what could be making the odd lights, perhaps another animal that was in the midst of being altered by the mysterious machine, that even now, all these centuries later was effecting the planet.  He stood there for nearly an hour doing his best to catch a glimpse of the lights, but the fading light and the distance of them made it nearly impossible for Marcus to see the source of the strange lights. A snapping of a twig near the base of a tree caught his attention and he whipped his head in that direction, for a moment he tensed, ready to run should the sound be caused by a large predator, but he quickly relaxed when he caught sight of the small white furred monkey standing there at the tree base, its head was cocked as it studied Marcus , his guess was the little monkey had never seen a human before. “Hey little guy, what are you doing here?” he asked. Wondering how the hell a monkey was wild in the western America’s.  He was no animal expert, but this looked like the spider monkeys he had seen on the various animal planet episodes he had so loved to watch. Marcus didn’t move, didn’t try to get closer and did his best to remain neutral and not a threat to the much smaller animal. After a short time, he figured that he had done a good job as the monkey turned to the tree, dismissing him.  As Marcus watched, the little monkey walked over grabbing two of the crystal spires and to his astonishment the simian’s fur began to glow, it seemed to draw power from the crystal, in fact if Marcus cleared his mind, he could almost hear the thrumming of the spire as the monkey continued to touch it.  The little spider monkey grew brighter and brighter the longer he held onto the crystals , after a time it released its grip, its full as bright as any flashlight Marcus had seen, turning for a last look at the lone human, it chirped a goodbye and launched itself up into the tree, soaring from branch to branch to join its fellow compatriots far above. “You don’t see that every day” Marcus said shaking his head. What other animals will I find on this trip he wondered continuing to watch the monkeys frolic above him.  Eventually he grew tired and retired to the tent. He lay there as sleep was a long time coming, he remembered the feeling he had gotten when getting close to what was left of the bunker, “I wonder” he said and closed his eyes, clearing his head he listened both with his mind and his ears, for a long time nothing came but as time went by he began to feel or hear, he couldn’t really tell a distant vibration, then another and yet another after that. Is that the crystals he wondered, were they putting off a sound or was he sensing the power coursing through them. No matter how he tried he couldn’t tell whether it was a sound or if it was something more mental. Eventually sleep took him, the thrumming of crystals and the strange creatures of the earth were forgetting as he slipped deeper into unconsciousness.  “Where are you fallen, where did your vessel come down?” came a voice, Marcus looked around but saw nothing but black, there was no light, no feeling as he seemed to float in an ethereal space, for a moment he thought the voice itself was his imagination when the disembodied voice came again, seeming to echo through his mind.  “Tell me where you are fallen, let me come to you, let me help you” came the voice again, Marcus could not feel ground beneath him, moving his hand to his face he could not see it, he felt with his palm came into contact with his nose, but with the absence of light he couldn’t even see his had inches from him. “Hello?” he called, the words seeming flat, a vast contrast to the echoing of the alien voice. He waited but no answer came so he called out again “Hey, who are you?” again his voice flat. “Where are you fallen, call out to me, use your gift and tell me where you are” the voice came again.  Marcus began to feel panic take over his thoughts as he tried to move, tried to see. His mouth opened to scream out, to call out and. He sat up with a start the scream escaping from his lips as his head hit the top of the tent, opening his eyes the light of morning played with the shadows of branches off of the fabric as the scream died a stillbirth in his throat. “A dream” he said, a smile of relief spreading over his face as he lay back down, allowing his body to calm and his heart to stop racing. “What the fuck” he breathed shaking his head at his own hysterics. “You have enough issues without freaking out Marc” he said to himself, after a time he calmed down, dressing he crawled out of the tent to the cold morning sun.  Surveying the forest, he studied the large old oaks and poplars, the forest going on for miles, most of the leaves had fallen from the trees, but there was still enough on the branches to give the forest color.  Crossing his arms, he braced himself as a light breeze played across the forest. It was a short time later as a fire roared warming him and breakfast had long since finished when the epiphany came. Sitting there he still had no answer on how to find civilization when suddenly the simplest solution popped into his head. “You idiot” he said shaking his head as he scrambled over to the pack and dug out the egg. He had since turned off Sentinel since the bunker but now needed her access to the ship.  Smiling he watched as the little egg pulsed red, then yellow and finally green. As the computer rendered woman appeared Marcus didn’t wait for Sentinel to give its familiar greeting. “Sentinel does the ship still have access to long range camera’s?” he asked and waited impatiently for the answer.  For the first time since waking Marcus was excited, I hope this works he thought as he willed the machine to speed up, to answer his request, the action was impudent, but made him feel a little better. The VI moved “Marcus, we still have full functionality over seventy percent of our available cameras to  utilize in analyzing land masses, weather and other events on the planet” Sentinel stated, her tone had an almost annoyed tone, if he didn’t know  better  he would think she was offended at his questioning of the ship’s capabilities.  Interesting he thought “What kind of information can we gain on the landscape, more importantly how is your ability to extrapolate a geometric analysis from Realtime photos of the land?” Marcus asked and could see the spark of interest in the VI’s eyes.  Could it be it was a bit more than a simple interface he wondered or was he merely anthropomorphizing the computer in a desperate attempt to develop a connection with another person.  He would need to watch that he thought, it would be too easy to fall into the thought process that Sentinel was a flesh and blood creature, well an emotional sentient one at the very least he corrected, looking at the silver outline of the female frame.  “That ability it available to us Marcus, by your command” Sentinel finished, waiting for the command that would send the computer and the ship into action. Taking a pause, he ordered his thoughts, he knew what he wanted but now he had to ensure he said it in such a way the computer did as well.  “Sentinel, I want you to comb the landscape, look for straight lines or other formations , tree removal or paths that are too symmetrical for nature, once found, analyze the probability of them being a human creation, then follow back the item in question and check the landscape for buildings or other signs of life” he finished, waiting with bated breath as Sentinel passed the information to the ship and waited for a response.  It seemed an agonizingly long time before the VI began to move once more. “We are more than capable of doing that, however because the age of the hardware, it will have to be done  carefully ,  this process will take , at the very least the remainder of the day Marcus” Sentinel finished and then waited.
